title: BREAKING NEWS: AI coding may not be helping as much as you think
description: METR (AI benchmarking nonprofit) ran a randomized control trial in early 2025 to test whether AI tools (primarily Cursor Pro) sped up experienced open-source developers. Shocking finding: Current AI tools actually slowed down task completion time by 19%, despite developers expecting 24% speed improvement and estimating 20% after completion. Study involved 245 tasks in mature projects with developers having 4.9 years average experience. Major caveat: Results may not generalize to smaller projects, less experienced developers, or different quality standards.
author: Gary Marcus

title: Ask HN: What explains the recent surge in LLM coding capabilities?
description: Hacker News discussion exploring explanations for sudden perceived improvements in LLM coding capabilities. Key insights: 1) RLVR (Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards) replacing RLHF - models can train without human feedback using unit tests and automated verification; 2) Better tool calling and fine-tuning on successful patterns from telemetry data; 3) Improved agentic frameworks and planning before coding; 4) Marketing hype during holidays amplified perceived improvements. Some argue it's incremental progress along same technical direction (scaling, better data, improved tooling) rather than fundamental breakthrough. Claude Code specifically noted for good research and planning before writing code.
author: orange_puff (Hacker News)

title: The New Experience of Coding with AI
description: Deep exploration of how AI code assistants are changing software engineering work. Covers: 1) Current functionality (accessing all project files, writing significant code chunks, 'reasoning' LLMs, agent tools); 2) Different developer responses - enthusiastic adopters embracing 'vibe coding' vs 'craftspeople' who find it troubling to their creative identity; 3) The seduction factor and ethical dilemmas (job security, skill atrophy, environmental costs of generative AI); 4) Cognitive dissonance developers feel between productivity demands and ethical concerns. Notes that AI assistants seem here to stay via open source alternatives even if major LLM providers struggle economically.
author: Stephanie Kirmer

title: State of AI in 2026: LLMs, Coding, Scaling Laws, China, Agents, GPUs, AGI
description: Lex Fridman Podcast episode #490 covering comprehensive state of AI in 2026. Topics include LLMs and coding capabilities, AI scaling laws, developments in China's AI ecosystem, agentic AI systems, GPU hardware, and progress toward AGI. 4+ hour discussion providing current perspectives on AI advancement and implications.
author: Lex Fridman with guests

title: A Survey on Code Generation with LLM-based Agents
description: Academic paper surveying how LLM-powered code generation agents are revolutionizing software development. Covers latest research on code generation paradigms, architectures, and evaluation methods for agentic AI coding systems.
author: Multiple Authors

title: My LLM coding workflow going into 2026
description: Addy Osmani shares insights on effective LLM coding workflows for 2026. Discusses how AI coding assistants became game-changers in 2025 and best practices for integrating them into development workflows.
